label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/big_rock.mdl, models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The outline is a plain square-cornered box in every view (sides.png, FRONT through BACK-RIGHT). A valve wheel's round rim, hub and spokes are absent in all ten views, so the silhouette does not match the brief's wheel.

M2.reason: Measured sizeOff is 0 and the extent is 32 x 32 x 24, so the 32-unit across size the brief gives is met. The brief gives no height for the wheel, so only the across size is checked here.

M3.reason: No parts are present. The brief's wheel has a hub, spokes and a rim, and the model is one solid block with none of them, in any view.

M4.reason: The whole block is one flat neutral grey with a noise texture. The brief's red paint is missing, and the worn-to-steel region at the rim is missing too.

M5.reason: There is no paint wear, markings or stripes at the rim or anywhere else. The only surface is a uniform noise texture with no features that the brief describes.

M6.reason: In lineup.png (B), the reproduction is an obvious grey cube beside the rock, the gib and the sphere. A player would not take it for a valve wheel, and no Half-Life prop of this size looks like it.

M7.reason: The model has no wheel orientation or front. Its upright, faced, standing pose cannot be a wheel's, since a valve wheel stands on its edge with a hub facing the player, and this block has neither.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty. The model has 12 triangles, which is well under twice the median of 62 for Half-Life's props of this size, and the block is closed with no open faces or floating parts in the views.
